notes: 33,754 bins over 15 chromosomes, int64 counts on disk that the cool writer narrows to int32. The h5 source sets fileWasH5, so the nan bin masking of cool.py:267-279 runs.
--enforce_integer on a matrix that already holds integers is inert, except that the sum attribute stays float64 because np.rint produces a float column that cooler sums before casting it.
A corrected float64 matrix, 1,252,980 stored pixels between 1.3e-05 and 0.12. The control for the case below.

The data destroying defect, pinned rather than fixed: every value is below 0.5, np.rint sends all 1,252,980 of them to zero, the file is written with sum 0 and the tool exits 0 without a warning. See test_hicConvertFormat.py:435 and the comment in cpp/tools/hicConvertFormat.cpp.
The reverse direction. The 14,845 nan bins the cool loader recovers heuristically end up in /nan_bins.
272 bins of int32 counts written as a dense gzipped table with no trailing newline. E0 is on the decompressed content: gzip stores a timestamp, so the compressed bytes can never match.
306 bins of float64, which is the case that exercises the float repr: a dense table of a float matrix prints '0.0' for every absent cell and the shortest round tripping decimal for every present one.
35,857 upper triangle entries. The declared output is the '.tsv' sidecar, because --outFileName names a file the tool never writes.
1,661,678 float64 values printed as text, the widest test of the float repr in the tier.
One based bin ids for the 35,857 stored entries plus a bed file of all 33,754 bins. Hicpro.save ignores pSymmetric and writes whatever is stored, which for an h5 source is the upper triangle.
The float64 variant, and the one bed file in the tier whose bins have unequal widths.
3,114 one megabase bins, 57,034 triplets of float64. The reader has to sum duplicate coordinates, as csr_matrix((data, (i, j))) does.

313,762 bins over 93 hg19 contigs from 8,688 input lines, of which 7,987 cells survive. Exercises the two quirks of the 2D-text path: an interval that straddles a bin boundary sets two cells, and a repeated pair keeps the last value rather than the sum.

Three resolutions under /resolutions. 50000 is the source resolution and is copied, the other two go through merge_bins; 200000 loses a chromosome that is too short to merge, so its nchroms is 14 and not 15. Also pins the metadata quirk: hic_metadata is consumed in place, so only the first resolution carries genome-assembly in its metadata attribute, and only the first writes hicmatrix's provenance onto the file root.

The same path from an h5 source, where none of the three resolutions equals the 5 kb source bin size so merge_bins runs three times. fileWasH5 is set, so the nan bins merge_bins recomputes are also the ones the cool writer masks with.

The other mcool branch (hicConvertFormat.py:331-344): no --resolutions, one group per input matrix named after its own bin size, the second matrix appended. Both inputs are at 5 kb, so the second replaces the first's group and the file ends with a single resolution. Also the only case where the output handler is built with neither pHiCInfo nor pEnforceInteger.

The memory reference of PLAN.md 4.5: Python peaks at 390 MB against a 19.9 MB working set, the budget is 1.3 * 19.9 + 64 = 90 MB. Also the correction path, where the 855 nan bins are masked, the factors are inverted into the weight column and divided back out of the counts.
